messages:
Maria C.: Hey team — running into a UX/permissions mismatch on the Console audit viewer for Private customers. Export button visible to some users who shouldn't have it.
Chetan: Which permission is leaking? audit.logs.export or a higher-level role?
Maria C.: Looks like it's tied to the old role 'admin:view' via group nesting. Repro steps: 1) log in as support_bot account 2) open Audit -> Events 3) toggle filters -> Export -> CSV.
Jordan: Oof. We've been migrating to granular perms (audit.logs.view / audit.logs.export). Could be an RBAC inheritance bug in the new policy evaluator.
Samir: Can you paste the exact policy for the affected group? might be a union vs intersection issue.
Maria C.: Policy snippet: ```
{
  "groups": ["support_team"],
  "allow": ["admin:view"],
  "deny": []
}
```
Chetan: The evaluator should normalize group policies then check explicit allows. If support_team is a member of helpdesk (which has admin:view), we may be accidentally treating inherited view as full export.
Kyla: UX question: Should we hide the export button entirely if user lacks audit.logs.export, or show disabled with tooltip? We need to standardize across Console.
Maria C.: Preference is disabled with tooltip and link to request permission (for enterprise flows). But critical: exports for Private/Customer-managed KMS must require extra checks.
Jordan: Good call. Also: export payload schema — customers expect timestamp + actor_id + resource_id, but we added metadata.* fields in schema v2. Some downstream parsing tools choke when metadata is nested JSON.
Samir: We should offer export formats: CSV flattened (metadata.* -> dotted columns), JSON lines, and raw JSON. Add a schema version header in CSV: `#audit_schema:v2` so customers can detect.
Chetan: For encryption, Private exports initiated from Console should be server-side encrypted with customer KMS if tenant has CMK enabled. Right now exports are stored temporarily in S3 with default provider key -> potential compliance gap.
Maria C.: Confirmed. Affected tenants: two beta customers on Private. They flagged that export files appear in S3 with AWS-managed key.
security-bot: NOTE: Incident created (#INC-2025-0477) when export key mismatch detected. Assigned to @Samir.
Samir: I'll scope a fix: 1) block export UI if user lacks audit.logs.export 2) fix policy evaluator inheritance bug 3) add server-side KMS selection and ensure CMK is used for export objects 4) add schema-version header and JSONL option 5) add audit event validation on export pipeline so malformed events are rejected.
Jordan: For event validation, we need a strict schema: required fields: `timestamp`, `actor_id`, `action`, `resource_type`, `resource_id`. Optional: `metadata` (map). If metadata contains nested objects, we either flatten or allow JSON in a single CSV column.
Kyla: Also add pagination cursor export: if user exports full date range (>100k events) we should stream JSONL rather than try to build huge CSV in memory. UX should show estimated size and warn about retention and encryption.
Maria C.: Timeline? Beta customers need this by next week or we'll escalate.
Samir: Hotfix for RBAC visibility and blocking export for unauthorized users by EOD tomorrow. KMS fix + schema header and JSONL streaming will be next week.
Chetan: Tests: add unit tests for policy evaluator (group nesting), integration tests for export with CMK, and an end-to-end on Private tenant that verifies exported object S3 key is encrypted with customer key id.
Jordan: Also add a quick CLI check: `redwood audit export --tenant T123 --format jsonl --dry-run` that validates permissions and prints export size estimate without creating file.
Maria C.: One more: customer-facing validation failures should surface in UI as an export failure with error code and link to support, not an opaque 500. Log the full event in internal audit (with redact) so security can triage.
Kyla: UX microcopy: "You don't have permission to export audit logs. Request access" and for CMK: "Export will be encrypted with your customer-managed key (CMK)."
Samir: I'll follow up with a PR that updates policy evaluator + export service. Tagging @Chetan and @Jordan for code review.
Chetan: ACK. I'll start writing testcases.
Maria C.: Thanks all — keeping this thread for status. If anyone finds other tenants with wrong export visibility ping here. :thumbsup:
security-bot: Incident #INC-2025-0477 status -> triage in progress.
